title: Dungeon Dive Hobbycast - E1 - Intro and Ranking of SoulsBorneRingKiro games
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KlnSnb7YFEY

The Hobbycast begins, and Daniel (@dungeondive) opens by explaining why it exists at all. He has cut his day job to three days a week and is trying to make the Dungeon Dive a full-time occupation — which needs several revenue streams — but the artistic reason matters more. He thinks holistically: board games remind him of books, books of music, music of film. YouTube's algorithm punishes that kind of range, so the podcast becomes the place to put it.

Then the main event: every modern FromSoftware game, ranked. He notes the community's obsession with credentials before wearily supplying his own, back to *King's Field II* on the PS1 (hated it) and *Otogi* on the Xbox (still owns both).

The ranking is *Dark Souls III* last — lazy fan-service, flat levels, a final boss out of an NES game — then *Sekiro*, then *Elden Ring*, and his reason is consistent and disarmingly honest: the games outran his reflexes, and 40 of his 100 *Elden Ring* hours weren't fun. Above them: *Demon's Souls* for level design, *Dark Souls* for the interconnected world and that first upward glance from Blighttown, *Dark Souls II* for being a game genuinely *about* memory, and *Bloodborne* at the top.

----

Is it more useful to hear a game ranked by someone who admits it beat them, or by someone who mastered it?
